Subject: Sudden latency and 503s on our Dedicated pool this morning

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 95th/99th percentile latency in our integration tests around 08:45 PDT this morning. A subset of calls to our generation endpoints returned 503s and a number of requests timed out. This only affects our Dedicated cluster (pool id: d-4892).

Key notes from our side:
- Spike started ~08:45, peaked at ~09:10, then intermittently persisted through the morning.
- Error rate ~2.3% at peak (normally <0.01%).
- Request patterns: many small, short-context calls (~20–40 tokens) from several worker shards.

Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing anything on your side? We can share logs if helpful.

Lena

Subject: Triage: KV-cache churn correlated with small-context burst traffic

Team / Lena,

Quick triage update from infra: we correlated the timeframe with high KV cache miss and eviction churn on pool d-4892. Preliminary findings:

- Around 08:40–09:15 PDT we saw a 18x increase in KV store evictions and a corresponding rise in GC/compaction activity on the serving nodes.
- The request pattern shows a large number of short-lived contexts (20–40 tokens), often switching between many different prefixes. That pattern leads to frequent KV cache flushes and low reuse, which increases memory pressure and causes thrashing.
- Thrashing led to transient spikes in CPU and allocation latency for the runtime, which is consistent with the observed 503s and timeouts.

Immediate mitigations we pushed (10:05–10:20):
- Bounded per-tenant KV footprint temporarily lowered from 4 GB->1.5 GB to reduce eviction storms.
- Enabled a short-lived sticky-sampling policy to prioritize hot prefixes and reduce churn.
- Increased request queue headroom on the affected nodes to reduce preemption.

Effect: error rate dropped from 2.3% to ~0.2% and 95th latency improved by ~45% within 10 minutes of changes.

Next steps:
- We'll attach a compact timeline and diagnostic bundle (kv-cache-analysis.txt) for your ops team.
- We want to test a targeted prefix-caching tweak on a canary subset of your traffic overnight.
- Engineering will propose a permanent knob to make the uploader/client request pattern less harmful (client-side batching or server hints).

I'll follow with the analysis file and proposed patch for review.

— Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

1) Canary test: 2028-06-01 23:00–02:00 PDT — deploy prefix-caching tweak to 10% of AdGrow traffic. Karthik will push the canary build and run targeted telemetry.
2) Playbook (short): if latency/error rate increases >0.5% during canary -> roll back within 10 minutes, increase per-tenant KV cap, and enable strict hot-prefix pinning. We attached timeline_adgrow.csv with the event markers.
3) Post-incident remediation: engineering to prepare remediation_patch.diff that hardens eviction heuristics and adds a client-signal header to mark short-burst traffic for different caching semantics.
4) Billing/credits: Ben, please propose a one-time usage credit to compensate for the outage window.
5) Customer comms: We'll send a consolidated incident summary after the postmortem is complete; interim status will be posted to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-06-kvcache-9842.

We will include the diagnostic bundle (attached) and a short list of client changes we recommend (light client-side batching or adding the server-hint header).
